front: How is Q5 (Paper 2) marked out of 40?
back: 24 marks for content and organisation (AO5), 16 for technical accuracy (AO6) — same split as Paper 1's Q5.

front: What should you decide first when planning a viewpoint answer?
back: Your position — you don't have to fully agree or disagree, a nuanced view can work well if argued clearly.

front: What's "counter-argument and rebuttal", and why use it?
back: Briefly acknowledging the other side, then showing why your view still stands — shows a controlled, convincing argument.
Grouping ideas or examples in threes for rhythm and emphasis.

front: Why does the form of the task matter (letter vs article vs speech)?
back: Each has its own conventions (greeting/sign-off, headline, direct audience address) and expected tone/formality.

front: What's a common weakness examiners flag in viewpoint writing?
back: A one-sided rant with no acknowledgement of the other side, or technique used with no real argument behind it.
